knowledge:
- key_parameters: x_list=A list of transposed gene expression matrices where rows represent samples and columns represent features ;; y_list=A list of survival data frames (containing time and event status) corresponding to the datasets in x_list ;; nFeatures=An integer specifying the number of features to be selected by the lasso regression model ;; newx=A gene expression matrix for independent validation or evaluation ;; newy=A survival object or data frame for independent validation or evaluation
- alternatives: Traditional merging of datasets followed by extensive batch correction methods (e.g., ComBat), which TOP avoids by using transfer learning strategies
- when_to_use: When you have multiple independent transcriptomics datasets from different platforms or cohorts and want to train a robust, transferable survival prediction model that generalizes well to independent validation data
- pitfalls: Input matrices must have identical feature names (e.g., gene symbols) across all datasets, requiring a pre-filtering step to find common genes ;; Expression matrices must be transposed so that samples are rows and features are columns before passing to TOP_survival ;; Sample IDs and ordering must match between the expression matrices (x_list) and survival data (y_list)

workflows.name: transferable_survival_modeling
workflows.intent: Build and evaluate a transferable survival model across multiple independent gene expression datasets.
input: list_ovarian_eset (a list of ExpressionSet objects containing gene expression and clinical metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify common features (genes) across all datasets ;; 2. Extract and align survival metadata (time and event status) ;; 3. Subset and transpose gene expression matrices to match survival samples and common genes ;; 4. Train the transferable survival model using TOP_survival ;; 5. Evaluate model performance (concordance index) using Surv_TOP_CI
workflows.code:
raw_gene_list <- purrr::map(list_ovarian_eset, rownames)
common_genes <- Reduce(f = intersect, x = raw_gene_list)
ov_pdata <- purrr::map(list_ovarian_eset, pData)
list_pdata <- list_ovarian_eset %>%
  purrr::map(pData) %>%
  purrr::map(tibble::rownames_to_column, var = "sample_id")

ov_surv_raw <- purrr::map(
  .x = list_pdata,
  .f = ~ data.frame(
    sample_id = .x$sample_id,
    time = .x$days_to_death %>% as.integer(),
    dead = ifelse(.x$vital_status == "deceased", 1, 0)
  ) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      time > 0,
      !is.nan(time),
      !is.nan(dead)
    )
)
ov_surv_y <- ov_surv_raw %>%
  purrr::map(~ .x %>%
    dplyr::select(-sample_id)) %>%
  purrr::map(~ Surv(time = .x$time, event = .x$dead))
ov_surv_exprs <- purrr::map2(
  .x = list_ovarian_eset,
  .y = ov_surv_raw,
  .f = ~ exprs(.x[common_genes, .y$sample_id])
)

ov_surv_tbl <- ov_surv_raw %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "data_source")
surv_list <- ov_surv_tbl %>%
  split(ov_surv_tbl$data_source)
surv_list <- lapply(surv_list, function(x) x[, 3:4])

surv_counts <- ov_surv_exprs %>% lapply(t)
surv_list <- surv_list[names(surv_counts)]
surv_model <- TOP_survival(
  x_list = surv_counts, y_list = surv_list, nFeatures = 10
)
conf_results <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(surv_counts), function(x) {
  Surv_TOP_CI(
    surv_model,
    newx = surv_counts[[x]], newy = surv_list[[x]]
  )$concordance
}))
